title: Composition square of intrinsic finite scalar tensorators
statement: Let $X$ be any scheme, $\ell$ a prime and $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ a finite extension. For $n\ge m\ge r\ge0$ use the ambient intrinsic derived categories at positive exponents $n+1,m+1,r+1$ and the normalized quotient scalar extensions $F,G,J$ [def-sf-etale-finite-coefficient-hom-arrow, lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus, def-coef-normalized-dvr-tower, def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. Write $T_n,T_m,T_r$ for their closed-record tensor functors, $\mu:T_nF\cong(F\times F)T_m$, $\nu:T_mG\cong(G\times G)T_r$, $\xi:T_nJ\cong(J\times J)T_r$ for the fixed quotient-calculus tensorators, and $\alpha:F G\cong J$ for finiteHomIntrinsicAssoc, the left-adjoint mate of normalized restriction composition. Then for all ambient $K,M$, $G(\mu_{K,M})\,\nu_{FK,FM}\,T_r(\alpha_K,\alpha_M)=\alpha_{T_n(K,M)}\,\xi_{K,M}$, with compositions written in diagram order. This is a tensor square, with no Hom comparison or invertibility claim about Hom.

proof.text: Choose flat-term K-flat models of the two tensor inputs. The normalized quotient calculus computes its tensorators by ordinary scalar balancing and its quotient adjunctions by extension/restriction of scalars. The prescribed left-adjoint associator is represented by successive multiplication of coefficients.

The signed cochain tensor coherence gives equality before localization, also for identity quotients and zero inputs. K-flat change of rings permits nonflat quotients. The monoidal derived comparison descends this equality; naturality with respect to the resolutions gives the square for every ambient pair.

theorem finiteHomIntrinsic_tensorComposition
    (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime] (E : Type u) [Field E] [Algebra (Padic l) E]
    [FiniteDimensional (Padic l) E] (X : Scheme.{u})
    {n m r : ℕ} (h : m ≤ n) (k : r ≤ m) (K M : normalizedDVRDerived l E X n) :
    let S := (coefficientDerivedSystemEvaluationCalculus l E X).choose
    let μ := S.quotientCalculus.tensor h
    let ν := S.quotientCalculus.tensor k
    let ξ := S.quotientCalculus.tensor (k.trans h)
    let α := finiteHomIntrinsicAssoc l E X h k
    let F := coefficientFiniteQuotientDerived l E X h
    let G := coefficientFiniteQuotientDerived l E X k
    G.map (μ.hom.app (K, M)) ≫ ν.hom.app (F.obj K, F.obj M) ≫
        (finiteIntrinsicClosed l E X r).tensor.map
          (Prod.mkHom (α.hom.app K) (α.hom.app M)) =
      α.hom.app ((finiteIntrinsicClosed l E X n).tensor.obj (K, M)) ≫
        ξ.hom.app (K, M)
